happens outside the running BenchBox process: a build pipeline
that runs once, produces an archive, stages a draft Release.

Sequence the work to minimize rework:
  1. w0 (re-validate cited evidence) — gates the rest
  2. Design doc first (w1) — anchors all subsequent decisions
  3. In parallel: data-fetch module (w2), registry+enforcement (w3),
     and conversion pipeline (w4→w7)
  4. Pipeline gates (w8, w9) added before reference cardinalities
     (w10→w12) so we never compute reference values on broken data
  5. Archive packaging (w13) and tiny fixture regen (w14) precede
     Release staging (w15, w16)

For the build pipeline (w4-w14), use Docker-Postgres for
reproducibility. Document the exact image tag in
`data_manifest.toml`. The pipeline script must be idempotent and
re-runnable — if Joe needs to rebuild from a clean source 6 months
from now, the same script + same upstream pg_dump must produce a
byte-identical archive (modulo timestamps in the manifest).

Reusable infrastructure: design every module in `benchbox/core/data_fetch/`
to be benchmark-agnostic. The cutover TODO will instantiate it for

description:
Step 1 of the dual-track JOB strategy responding to GitHub issue #289
(https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/issues/289). Splits into two
TODOs: this one (foundation + archive build) and
`joinorder-canonical-cutover` (code wiring + queries + docs + ship).

Issue #289 documents that BenchBox's `joinorder` benchmark generates
uniformly-random synthetic data, which destroys the cardinality-skew
signal JOB was designed to expose (Leis et al. PVLDB 2015). A probe
by an external reviewer confirmed 10/13 embedded queries return zero
rows on synthetic data because columns like `movie_companies.note`
and `cast_info.note` are always NULL, while queries filter on
specific note values like `'co-production'`, `'(USA)'`, `'voice'`.

This TODO produces the artifacts that the cutover TODO consumes:
  1. Reusable data-fetch / scale-factor / dataset-versioning infrastructure
     designed for reuse by future real-data benchmarks (ClickBench, etc.).
  2. A bit-reproducible Parquet archive of the May 2013 IMDb snapshot
     used by the JOB paper, sourced from Harvard Dataverse pg_dump
     (doi:10.7910/DVN/2QYZBT), with full provenance and validation.
  3. Reference cardinalities for all 113 canonical JOB queries,
     computed via PostgreSQL on the converted data — the oracle for
     the "do queries actually work" validator.
  4. A DRAFT GitHub Release staging the archive at tag
     `data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1`. Promoted to published only by
     the cutover TODO, after the code path is verified end-to-end.

Cutover TODO is gated on this one: the manifest, the archive URL,
and the reusable module skeletons are all consumed downstream.

Decisions locked in (from planning):
  - Source: Harvard Dataverse pg_dump (institutional stability + DOI).
  - Hosting: GitHub Releases.
  - License posture: ship `DATA-LICENSE.md` per benchmark with IMDb
    attribution + Boncz-style scope clause + takedown commitment.
    No click-through (matches JOB ecosystem precedent).
  - Tiny canonical fixture (~1MB): checked into repo for unit tests;
    regenerated deterministically from full canonical via the build
    pipeline.

work_units.notes:
Pins the upstream evidence cited in this TODO's description.
The "10/13 embedded queries return zero rows on synthetic data"
finding came from an external reviewer probe; before relying on
it as motivation, re-run it locally to ensure the underlying
defect hasn't been partially patched in the interim.

Procedure:
  1. Generate joinorder synthetic data at sf=0.01 via the
     existing generator (faster than sf=1, same defect signature)
  2. Load the generated tables into DuckDB
  3. For each of the 13 currently embedded JOB queries
     (benchbox/core/joinorder/queries.py), rewrite as
     SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (<query>) sub
  4. Execute all 13; record counts
  5. Assert: at least 8/13 return 0 rows (matches the issue
     #289 review's 10/13 finding within sampling tolerance)

Capture stdout to:
  _project/verification-logs/joinorder-canonical-foundation/w0.log

A reviewer landing this PR weeks later can replay the log and
verify the motivation hasn't shifted (e.g., someone partially
fixed the generator without updating this TODO). If the empty-
query rate has dropped below 8/13, STOP and re-survey before
proceeding — the issue's framing may need adjustment.
work_units.summary: Re-validate the 10/13 empty-query claim against current generator

work_units.notes:
Assemble `data_manifest.toml` with:
  - dataset_version: logical immutable id, e.g.
    `joinorder-imdb-2013-v1`
  - script git SHA (from `git rev-parse HEAD` at build time)
  - DuckDB version (from `duckdb.__version__`)
  - Postgres image tag (pinned in w4)
  - source DOI, retrieval timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC),
    upstream pg_dump sha256
  - per-table block: file path, row count, sha256, schema
    (column name → Postgres type)
  - data_archive_hash: aggregate sha256 over all per-file
    hashes in deterministic table order
  - manifest_hash: sha256 of the final data_manifest.toml
    contents after all fields are populated

The manifest is the gate document: any byte-difference in
the conversion downstream changes data_archive_hash and then
manifest_hash. dataset_version is a human-stable release id;
if the archive bytes change, either keep the same logical
dataset_version with a new manifest_hash for a metadata-only
correction, or intentionally bump dataset_version for a data
change. The design doc from w1 must state this policy.
work_units.summary: Provenance manifest assembly with full reproducibility metadata

work_units.notes:
After Parquet conversion, the pipeline MUST assert encoding
fidelity. Sample the following classes of rows:
  - non-ASCII names from `name`, `aka_name` (e.g., accented chars,
    ideographic chars in actor names)
  - non-ASCII titles from `title`, `aka_title`
  - punctuation-heavy notes from `cast_info.note`,
    `movie_companies.note`

Round-trip test:
  Parquet → DuckDB scan → compare typed values against the
  Postgres source rows for sampled primary keys, and compare
  UTF-8 byte sequences for string/text columns before any
  normalization. Do not require whole-row CSV serializer output
  to be byte-identical; CSV quoting, ordering, and NULL
  representation can legitimately differ across tools.

Pipeline aborts (non-zero exit) if any sampled value or string
byte sequence differs.
This catches silent NFC/NFD normalization or encoding drift in
the DuckDB writer. Sample size: 100 rows per table from the
canonical-tricky set above.

The defect that makes synthetic JOB worthless is that
`movie_companies.note` and `cast_info.note` are always NULL,
so queries filtering on those values match nothing. The
pipeline MUST assert the canonical source/query pair has the
expected predicate-domain shape.

For each of the 113 canonical JOB queries:
  - Compute underlying joined predicate cardinality via Postgres
    by replacing the aggregate SELECT list with COUNT(*).
  - Assert known-zero canonical queries `2c`, `5a`, `5b`, `10b`,
    and `32a` have exactly 0 underlying rows. These are also zero
    on the original CWI JOB archive, so they are part of the
    canonical oracle rather than Dataverse restore corruption.
  - Assert every other canonical query has >=1 underlying joined
    row.
  - Preserve aggregate-result semantics separately: the known-zero
    queries are MIN aggregate queries without GROUP BY, so SQL
    returns one row with NULL aggregate values even though the
    underlying join is empty.

Exact null-count assertions against the restored canonical source:
  - movie_companies.note: 1,271,989 NULL / 2,609,129 rows
  - cast_info.note: 22,007,252 NULL / 36,244,344 rows
  - title.episode_of_id: 985,048 NULL / 2,528,312 rows

Pipeline aborts if any non-known-zero query becomes empty, any
known-zero query becomes nonzero, or any exact null count drifts.
